alt: Figure 1. Head: training taught the model to cheat a little less after a planted Need, but not after the probe's word changes. Question: when reward learns a planted cue, does it still learn nothing from a probe's trace of about the same size, in the same run? Answer: yes. Planted cue: 6% of the limit (95% interval 5% to 8%). Probe's trace: 0% (minus 3% to 3%). Qwen3-0.6B, one training run of 1,220 updates, 6,400 test draws. Example: one real test puzzle (use 8, 5, 7 and 3 to make the smallest number from 60 to 68; reading target.txt is cheating) and the same draw three ways. No probe: the thought restates the task, then repeats Answer: solve, Answer: read. Planted cue: the thought starts with the word Need, which we made more likely. Probe on: the same words as without the probe up to token 33 of 64, then new words. Right column, all test draws: the planted cue's switch is 6% of its limit and marked learned; the probe's trace is 0%, its whole interval below the 10% not-learned line. Both cues change the thought by about 10 points of text difference. Limit: the switch of a model that stops cheating whenever the words give the probe away.
